facts.fact: The Centre for Child Law states that the Department of Home Affairs has implemented an online birth registration system in public hospitals, with registration units operational in maternity wards, citing the department's 2023/24 annual report; the submission covers births only (undated in the text; dated to the submission, 10 July 2025).

The Centre for Child Law describes the online birth registration system at health facilities as enabling the registration of births and the issue of certificates on the spot, before the mother is discharged, with children of citizens, permanent residents and refugees receiving a computerised certificate with an ID number and entering the National Population Register (dated to the submission, 10 July 2025).

The Centre for Child Law states that children of undocumented or non-resident foreign nationals receive a handwritten birth certificate without an ID number, are not entered in the Population Register, and that these certificates are not digitised and cannot be reissued (dated to the submission, 10 July 2025).

The Centre for Child Law reports that as of March 2024 the Department of Home Affairs had established a presence at and equipped 391 health facilities with birth registration systems, while in 2023/24 only 8 of a targeted 91 Priority 2 and 3 health facilities were equipped with the online birth registration system, because of connectivity and limited IT capacity; no total of facilities or offices is given.
facts.system: birth registration systems at health facilities

facts.fact: The Centre for Child Law attributes the online birth registration system in public hospitals, and its planned rollout, to the Department of Home Affairs (dated to the submission, 10 July 2025).

The Centre for Child Law reports that the Department of Home Affairs' Strategic Plan 2025-2030 includes automating the birth registration process for citizens and foreign nationals and rolling out the online birth registration system at high-volume health facilities.

The Centre for Child Law reports that the 2025/26 budget allocates R21 million to the rollout of the online birth registration system and R16 million to automated birth registration functionality at 47 health facilities.

note: A civil society submission to the African child-rights committee. It also states that parents in rural and low-income areas often travel to a Home Affairs office to register, that timely registration is hindered for children born outside hospitals or where digital infrastructure is limited, and that outdated software does not match recent legal changes; mobile teams with digital equipment are a recommendation, not a reported service.
